not_applicable.reason: Only the part about a worker or a child process, case mask-009. ahd starts no child process and passes the credential to no other program. The rest of the rule applies and is met.

Only the part about files and folders that a tool writes, cases perm-001, perm-002 and perm-003. ahd only reads profiles and config files and writes no credential. The warning for a file that others can read applies and is met.

differences.summary: ahd uses the first of these: a profile from --profile or AA_PROFILE, all four AHD_ variables, a config file from --config or ./config.json, the variables ORG_ID, CLIENT_ID, SECRET and SCOPES, and the .env file in the working folder. So ./config.json wins over the plain variables and over .env. --config together with AA_PROFILE, or together with all four AHD_ variables, stops the command. ahd prints the notice plain_variables_not_used or dotenv_and_config_differ when the order of the standard would give another credential.

When only some of the AHD_ variables are set, each one replaces the same key of the config file, and ahd prints the notice mixed_sources. A partial set of the plain variables, or a partial .env file, beside a config file is not read, and ahd prints the notice partial_source_skipped. When the AHD_ names and the plain names hold different values, ahd uses the AHD_ names and prints the notice variable_forms_differ.
